title.narrative: EcoR.E.S Crescita economica rispettosa dell’ambiente, inclusiva e giusta
EcoR.E.S. Eco-friendly, inclusive and fair economic growth in Bosnia and Herzegovina

description.narrative: L’iniziativa promossa da 26 partner, tra enti pubblici, privati, aziende e OSC locali ed italiane, ha l’obiettivo di incentivare, secondo un approccio intersezionale, una crescita economica, duratura, equa, inclusiva e sostenibile, un'occupazione piena, produttiva ed un lavoro dignitoso in Bosnia ed Erzegovina (d’ora in poi BiH), in linea con le richieste di adeguamento UE. L’iniziativa ha il fine di contrastare la rate sulla disoccupazione, attraverso i suoi tre risultati: formazione; creazione di posti di lavoro; rimozione degli ostacoli all’inclusione delle donne, garantendo la parità di genere, e dei disabili, di rivitalizzare il mercato del lavoro e lo sviluppo del commercio, contribuendo alla mitigazione del cambiamento climatico, alla tutela della biodiversità, sviluppando la partecipazione alla vita democratica. Caratteristiche dell’iniziativa sono l’approccio intersezionale, che indica una crescita economica che non può essere intesa come separata dalla tutela ambientale, dalla parità di genere, da principi di equità e eticità, qui rappresentati da Fondazione Finanza Etica, e da un alto tasso di innovazione sociale sistemica, applicata alla formazione, alle startup di impresa e alla presa in carico delle vulnerabilità. L’efficacia della formazione è determinata anche da una ricerca, condotta dall’Agenzia NERDA,sul disallineamento tra le competenze possedute dai lavoratori e le reali necessità delle imprese locali (causa dell’indebolimento del mercato del lavoro) facilitando un concreto sbocco occupazionale. L’iniziativa prevede la creazione di percorsi formativi di qualità, professionali, on the job, identificati sulla base delle strategie di sviluppo delle Regioni coinvolte e sviluppati anche in collaborazione con imprese private, e 3 Università, gli attori del Sistema Italia rappresentati dall’Associazione Imprese Italiane in BiH, in linea con l’esigenza (Report UE 23, UNESCO e UNICEF 23) di migliorare la qualità dell'istruzione e della formazione per sostenere una crescita economica a lungo termine. Tali percorsi includono tirocini retribuiti e periodi di permanenza in Italia. L’iniziativa aumenta l’occupazione verde attraverso la creazione e il rafforzamento di 2 start up di impresa, il matching dei giovani con il mondo del lavoro e azioni di emersione dal lavoro informale, che porteranno alla registrazione di nuove ditte. Le start-up, volte alla produzione artigianale e agroalimentare, saranno gestite, dopo un percorso di incubazione di impresa, da giovani disabili della scuola speciale JU di Tuzla e dalle donne in vulnerabilità economica e sociale di Srebrenica. A tale riguardo è significativo il coinvolgimento del mondo profit italiano come C.O.R.A.Lab SRL, spin-off dell’Università di Urbino, Perché ci Credo SRL, Confartigianato Lecce, che sosterranno il potenziamento delle piccole imprese, selezionate anche in base al loro potenziale impatto sociale, economico e ambientale, garantito da una ricerca di mercato preliminare da parte di Nerda, dalla qualità della formazione, e da canali di distribuzione e vendita già individuati, in Italia e in BiH. Verrà potenziato il Centro per l’Accessibilità dell’Istituto Pedagogico del KT, e adottato il gender mainstream approach. Sono incluse azioni sostenibili nel tempo, volte ad alleviare l’onere sulle donne. The initiative promoted by 26 partners, including public and private bodies, companies and local and Italian CSOs, has the objective of encouraging, according to an intersectional approach, long-lasting, fair, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full employment, productive and decent work in Bosnia and Herzegovina (henceforth BiH), in line with EU compliance requests. The initiative aims to combat the unemployment rate, through its three results: training; job creation; removal of obstacles to the inclusion of women, ensuring gender equality, and of disabled people, to revitalize the labor market and the development of trade, contributing to the mitigation of climate change, the protection of biodiversity, developing participation in democratic life. Characteristics of the initiative are the intersectional approach, which indicates an economic growth that cannot be understood as separate from environmental protection, gender equality, principles of equity and ethics, represented here by Fondazione Finanza Etica, and a high rate of systemic social innovation, applied to training, business startups, taking in charge all vulnerabilities. The effectiveness of the training is also determined by research conducted by the North East Development Agency on the misalignment between the skills possessed by workers and the real needs of local businesses (cause of the weakening of the labor market), facilitating a concrete employment opportunity. The initiative involves the creation of quality, professional, on-the-job training courses, identified on the basis of the development strategies of the Regions involved and also developed in collaboration with private companies, 3 Universities, the actors of the Italian System; represented by the Association of Italian Companies in BiH, in line with the need (EU Report 23, UNESCO and UNICEF 23) to improve the quality of education and training to support a long-term economic growth. These paths include paid internships and periods of stay in Italy. The initiative increases green employment through the creation and strengthening of n. 2 business start-ups and through the matching of young people with the world of work and actions to highlight informal work, which will lead to the registration of new companies. The start-ups, aimed at artisanal and agri-food production, will be managed, after a business incubation process, by disabled young people from the JU special school in Tuzla and by women in economic and social vulnerability from Srebrenica. In this perspective, is very significant the involvement of the Italian profit world, such as C.O.R.A.Lab SRL, a spin-off of the Urbino University, Perché ci credo SRL, Confartigianato Lecce, which will support the strengthening of small businesses, also selected on the basis of their potential social, economic and environmental impact, guaranteed by preliminary market research by Nerda, by the quality of training, and by distribution and sales channels already identified in Italy and Bosnia. The initiative Allegato 2_Modello Documento Unico di Progetto_DUP_Bando Promossi 2023 8 involves actions aimed at removing the obstacles that limit training participation and entry into the job market for disadvantaged people, in particular women and disabled people (one of the most marginalized categories in the country). The Accessibility Center of the KT Pedagogical Institute will be strengthened and the gender mainstream approach will be adopted. Sustainable actions aimed at alleviating the burden on women are included. The involvement of the Pedagogical Institute, Leptire and Anfass is a guarantee of the representativeness of the interests of disabled people in the project. Actions to strengthen the capacities of local NGOs are provided to ensure multiplier effects. The initiative, as an expression of a broad partnership rooted in the territory, was born from a participatory approach and promotes generative actions, which will produce long-term effects

tag.narrative: Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls
Achieve higher levels of economic productivity through diversification, technological upgrading and innovation, including through a focus on high-value added and labour-intensive sectors
By 2020, substantially reduce the proportion of youth not in employment, education or training
By 2030, achieve full and productive employment and decent work for all women and men, including for young people and persons with disabilities, and equal pay for work of equal value

By 2030, eliminate gender disparities in education and ensure equal access to all levels of education and vocational training for the vulnerable, including persons with disabilities, indigenous peoples and children in vulnerable situations
By 2030, ensure equal access for all women and men to affordable and quality technical, vocational and tertiary education, including university
By 2030, substantially increase the number of youth and adults who have relevant skills, including technical and vocational skills, for employment, decent jobs and entrepreneurship
Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all
Ensure women’s full and effective participation and equal opportunities for leadership at all levels of decision-making in political, economic and public life

Promote development-oriented policies that support productive activities, decent job creation, entrepreneurship, creativity and innovation, and encourage the formalization and growth of micro-, small- and medium-sized enterprises, including through access to financial services
Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all
